problem_statement: A test that selects the test_utils_main_exit_cb module and provides a function test_utils_main_exit_cb(int res) should be able to have the integer result of the program's main reported to that callback after main returns, so it can print SUCCESS or FAILED based on that result. Today selecting this module does not build. This lets a test that does not provide its own main still report success or failure from the entry-point's result.

problem_statement_fixed: A test that selects the test_utils_main_exit_cb module and provides a function test_utils_main_exit_cb(int res) should be able to have the integer result of the program's main reported to that callback after main returns, so it can print SUCCESS or FAILED based on that result. Today selecting this module does not build. The module must be registered as a pseudomodule named test_utils_main_exit_cb so that it can be selected with USEMODULE += test_utils_main_exit_cb, and the callback's public signature is void test_utils_main_exit_cb(int res). Selecting the module reports the value returned by the linked main, passing the value unchanged, with 0 meaning success and any nonzero value meaning failure. This lets a test that does not provide its own main still report success or failure from the entry-point's result, provided another part of the build supplies main. In particular, the libfixmath unit tests should be adapted to this mechanism: when test_utils_main_exit_cb is selected by a libfixmath unit-test consumer, that consumer need not provide main or call the unit tests itself; the libfixmath unit-test target/package must supply a main that runs the unit tests and returns a status value, so the callback can print SUCCESS or FAILED based on that result.
